listing.name: Gothic II: Night of the Raven (OpenGothic)
listing.summary: Play Gothic II: Night of the Raven with OpenGothic and your own original game files.
listing.original_game_title: Gothic II: Night of the Raven

steps.title: Prepare the Night of the Raven runtime and data
steps.instruction: Use a complete permitted OpenGothic Windows copy and your own Gothic II: Night of the Raven data. Select native Gothic2Notr.exe with its matching resources/libraries. Gothic I, Gothic II Classic and existing 32-bit Union/AST/Ikarus plugins do not inherit compatibility from this route. Finish setup upstream rather than selecting an installer or a helper.

steps.title: Preserve the actual working directory as well as game data
steps.instruction: Retain the creating working directory and established literal -g argument pointing to the actual absolute Gothic II data root, if used. Automatic discovery is not a reason to change a working data selection. Finish setup upstream and start and quit the copy before registration. The ordinary prepared launch uses no arguments. Keep any literal arguments your existing copy needs.

warnings: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.
Before updating the game, keep a copy of its working files and every location containing saved data. Choosing a different executable does not give it a separate profile.
Preserve the complete creating working directory, actual original-data root, every save/config/mod and unknown file; do not assume the original vendor save directory contains all OpenGothic state.

references.title: OpenGothic settings and save locations
references.instruction: The selected Windows code uses working-directory Gothic.ini and log.txt, separately from original System/Gothic.ini, and writes save_slot_0.sav/save_slot_N.sav relative to the working directory. Preserve the complete creating working directory, actual original-data root, every save/config/mod and unknown file; do not assume the original vendor save directory contains all OpenGothic state.

presentation.manual_preparation: Install your own Gothic II: Night of the Raven in the default Steam or Akella Gothic II folder under Windows Program Files before Play. Keep the original files in that separate installation. OpenGothic finds those files itself. If you need an explicit -g path, use the separate prepared-copy route. This Windows x64 Preview route preserves local Gothic.ini, numbered save slots and the F11 capture dbg.png. Startup and crash logs stay with their runtime version. Rollback carries current saves and does not establish older-version save compatibility. Gothic I, Gothic II Classic and 32-bit Union plugins need a different setup.

data_locations: the prepared working directory containing Gothic.ini and save slots
the separately owned original Gothic II installation
